gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.lede: Goal: install one official scenario skill into your agent and run a real analysis once.
gettingStarted.boundaryTitle: Analysis is not on this site
gettingStarted.boundaryBody: Openwisdom provides skill packages and install paths. Model calls, context, and billing stay in the agent you already use.
gettingStarted.boundaryDetail: The catalog helps you discover and install. CLI/MCP are package managers only (search / install / update / list)—they never call a model.
gettingStarted.installBody: CLI and MCP support one-command installs via npm; you can also clone from GitHub or copy manually. Full paths live on the
gettingStarted.installNote: CLI is available via npx openwisdom. GitHub and manual paths remain as alternatives.
gettingStarted.firstSkillBody: Start with the official scenario skill for a macro scan workflow:
gettingStarted.invokeBody: Open Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or your daily agent. Trigger the skill per its SKILL.md (name or description match). Run the flow on your own material.
gettingStarted.invokeTipBody: Your agent loads the skill instructions and produces a structured analysis draft—not a chat box on this website.
verifyItems: The skill folder appears under your agent’s skills path (e.g. .claude/skills/ or project config).
The agent can list or retrieve macro-scan (or the slug you installed).
After one full run you have reviewable output, not a hosted session log on this site.

faqPage.title: FAQ
faqPage.lede: Boundaries, install locations, language policy, and telemetry. Dense install steps live on the Install hub.

items.q: Does Openwisdom host analysis or web chat?
items.a: No. There is no in-browser AI analysis session. Skills install into your agent; your agent and model execute them.

items.q: Do CLI or MCP call a large language model?
items.a: No. They are package managers: search / install / update / list. No run command, no hosted sessions, no model API keys.
It depends on your agent and install scope (project or global). CLI/MCP write to that harness’s skills directory; manual install means you copy into the matching path. See the Install hub.

items.q: How do I update an installed skill?
items.a: Use npx openwisdom update (or the MCP update tool). You can also re-clone/pull the repo or overwrite the skill folder.

items.q: UI is bilingual—must skill bodies be bilingual too?
items.a: No. Site UI is zh/en; skill body language follows the contributor. The catalog shows content language for filtering.

items.q: My agent does not see the skill I just installed
items.a: Confirm the path matches the harness config, reload the agent, and check the slug. If it still fails, open a GitHub Issue with agent type and install method.

items.q: Is install heat required? Does it write into SKILL.md?
items.a: No on both. Heat is side-channel stats from web downloads and successful CLI/MCP installs; failures do not block install. Heat never mutates skill sources. Opt out with --no-telemetry or env vars.

items.q: Can I install from the monorepo instead of npm?
items.a: Yes. Contributors can build packages/cli and packages/mcp from source and point OPENWISDOM_SKILLS_ROOT at a local skills tree. For everyday use, prefer npx openwisdom and npx -y openwisdom-mcp from the public registry.

items.q: Is popular the default catalog sort?
items.a: No. Default sort stays featured. Popular is optional when heat data exists. Heat reflects recent install/download activity—not academic quality.

items.q: Does the changelog use version numbers?
items.a: Early notes use capability waves (e.g. 2026-07 site docs wave) for shipped surfaces. GitHub commits and Releases remain the full record—we do not put on fake version theater on the site.

authoringPage.title: Authoring
authoringPage.lede: How to write skills that can be discovered, installed, and reviewed: one directory per unit, clear layers, catalog-friendly frontmatter, and community PRs into community/.
unitBody: A skill is a directory: required SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body), optional assets/ (templates, diagrams, appendices).
The skills/ tree in git is the content source of truth. The site catalog and CLI/MCP share a generated index—do not invent skill metadata only on the website.
Install copies the whole directory into the user chosen agent skills path. Analysis always runs in the user agent, not on this site.
authoringPage.scenarioBody: A full analysis job: when to use it, inputs and steps, expected output, bias and boundary checks. Official v1 scenarios include macro-scan, personal-anchor, and metacognition-audit. Scenarios should cite references instead of embedding long theory essays.
authoringPage.referenceBody: Compact theory cards reusable across scenarios: definition, applicability bounds, common misuse, and reviewable points. Disciplines typically cover psychology, sociology, history, political-science, and economics. Official vs community is provenance, not a second product.
authoringPage.frontmatterIntro: Metadata powers catalog filters, agent discovery, and install validation. Exact fields follow the repo schema and contribute template. Community skills usually need:
frontmatterItems: name: kebab-case stable id aligned with the catalog (id optional; defaults to name)
description: short description for agents and discovery
scope: community for community contributions—do not self-label official
language: body language (zh / en / …); follows the contributor—do not force bilingual bodies
tags, version, references: discovery, change tracking, and scenario cite chains (per schema)
authoringPage.frontmatterNote: Site UI is zh/en; skill body language is the contributor choice. For exact field names, required keys, and validation, see the repo schema / contribute guide. Heat and install stats never write into SKILL.md.
scenarioTips: Open with when to use it and when not to—avoid universal-analysis tone.
Make steps executable: inputs, ordered agent actions, structured outputs.
Spell out bias / evidence / counterexample checks, and cite references instead of rewriting a textbook.
Outputs should be human-reviewable (outline, assumptions, uncertainties), not slogan conclusions.
Mirror official scenario structure and tone (e.g. macro-scan) so the skill stays installable and invokable.
referenceTips: Lead with a short definition, then applicability and non-applicability.
Call out common misuse and over-extension so agents and humans can correct course.
Keep card length: reusable across scenarios, not a standalone essay.
Ground terms in disciplinary context; use tags / disciplines for discovery when needed.
Body language may match the contributor; keep summary and frontmatter catalog-friendly.
prSteps: Fork the repo and clone locally.
Add a skill directory under skills/community/ with SKILL.md (and optional assets/).
Self-check frontmatter and body: layer / scope, bounds, and whether an agent can trigger it.
Open a PR into community/: state intent, audience, and known limits.
Revise from review; after merge, the catalog pipeline indexes it (no web upload).
authoringPage.prWarning: v1 has no web upload or moderation backend. External contributions default to community/. Do not edit official/ unless a maintainer invites you. Full flow lives on the contribute guide.

privacy.heading: Privacy & telemetry
privacy.lede: Install heat is anonymous stats used for catalog ranking. Stats never write into skill source files; install still works if you turn telemetry off.
collectItems: skillId (must be on the catalog allowlist) and event type (e.g. CLI/MCP install success, web download, copy-install command)
Timestamps and day-bucket counters (for 30-day and all-time heat)
CLI/MCP client version, plus an optional short-lived session id for de-duplication
Optional meta: providers list and install scope (project / global)
notCollectItems: Name, email, account, or login identity
Machine name, full home-directory paths, or other host identifiers
User-level profiles, ad tracking, or install history that can pinpoint a person
privacy.optOutHeading: How to turn off CLI / MCP telemetry
optOutItems: Environment: OPENWISDOM_NO_TELEMETRY=1 (CLI, MCP session env, or shell)
CI: CI=true or CI=1 defaults telemetry off to avoid pipeline spam
No report is sent when OPENWISDOM_TELEMETRY_URL is unset
privacy.optOutEnvNote: Copyable env form (same gate for CLI and MCP):
privacy.urlBody: CLI and MCP only POST when a report URL is configured. Production should point at this site’s telemetry route:
privacy.urlHint: Replace example.com with your deployment host. Web collection uses same-origin /api/telemetry and does not need this env var.
privacy.heatBody: installs (30d) only reflects recent install/download activity—not theoretical rigor, applicability bounds, or citability. Default catalog sort remains featured; popular is an optional view when heat data exists.
privacy.copyHeading: Copy-command is not on the main rank
privacy.copyBody: Copying an install command on the web does not count toward install heat. Main rank uses successful CLI/MCP installs and web downloads.
privacy.purposeBody: Improve catalog ranking and help maintainers prioritize updates. No account required.

conceptsPage.title: Concepts
conceptsPage.lede: Openwisdom is a layered social-science Agent Skills library: scenario workflows cite discipline references; the catalog helps you discover and install; analysis runs in your own agent.
layersBody: Content is organized in two layers—not a flat pile of prompts.

A scenario skill is a runnable analysis workflow: when to use it, step order, expected output, and bias/evidence checks. Example: the official scenario macro-scan for a macro scan of situations and systems.

A reference is a discipline theory/method card: definition, applicability bounds, common misuse, and how scenarios should cite it. References are usually building blocks, not full end-to-end runs on their own. Examples: a psychology card such as confirmation-bias, or a sociology card such as collective-action.
Why layers: scenarios own how this analysis proceeds; references own whether the concepts are clear and not misused. One scenario can cite many references; one reference can support many scenarios.
layersTableRows: Runnable analysis workflow; e.g. macro-scan, personal-anchor, metacognition-audit
Discipline theory/method card; e.g. confirmation-bias, collective-action; cited by scenarios
libraryBody: Openwisdom is a single skills library: scenarios, references, and listed entries share one catalog and the same CLI/MCP semantics.
Repo paths under skills/ still help maintenance and PRs (e.g. community/ for external contributions)—that is engineering layout, not three storefronts on the website.
libraryPoints: Recommended scenarios and discipline references are maintained and tied to the product narrative
External contributions default via GitHub PR into the skills tree and join the same catalog
Skill body language follows the contributor; site UI stays zh/en
runtimeBody: Openwisdom has three coupled surfaces: GitHub (source of truth for skills), the bilingual catalog site (discover, filter, detail, install guidance), and CLI/MCP package managers (search / install / update / list).
The website is for reading, filtering, and obtaining install paths. It is not an analysis chat and does not host sessions.
CLI and MCP only package-manage: they install skills into a coding agent you already use. They do not call models, have no run command, and need no model API keys.
After install, invoke skills in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or your daily agent per SKILL.md. Model calls, context, and billing stay in your agent and model budget.
conceptsPage.runtimeCalloutTitle: Analysis is not on this site
conceptsPage.runtimeCalloutBody: Openwisdom ships method and packaging; thinking runs in your agent and model. A hosted analysis session on the web would be outside this product boundary.
catalogBody: The Skills catalog presents the library as a filterable index. Common facets include layer (scenario / reference), discipline, content language, and default featured sort.
Filter by layer when you need a workflow (scenario) versus a concept card (reference).
There is no Official / Community / Curated facet: every entry belongs to one library.

Install heat (when shown) is a side-channel activity signal for installs/downloads—not an academic quality score, and it never writes into SKILL.md. Default sort remains featured; see privacy docs for telemetry detail.

cliPage.title: CLI & MCP
cliPage.lede: Openwisdom ships two skill package-manager surfaces: a human terminal CLI and MCP tools for agent sessions. They share the same catalog and install semantics. Neither calls a model or runs analysis.
cliPage.statusBody: openwisdom and openwisdom-mcp are published on npm (0.1.0+). Use npx openwisdom for the CLI and npx -y openwisdom-mcp for MCP. The monorepo remains an optional path for contributors who build from source. We do not claim install counts or production volume metrics.
cliBody: The CLI is for humans in a terminal: search the shared catalog, copy skill directories into the skills roots of the coding agents you choose, and list or update what is already installed.
The command surface is fixed: search / install / update / list. There is no run command, no hosted session, and no model API key. Analysis always runs in your agent on your model budget.
Interactive mode can multi-select harnesses; scripts and CI should pass -y and explicit --providers. For denser install paths and copyable command blocks, use the Install hub.
cliPage.cliInstallExample:
npx openwisdom install
npx openwisdom install macro-scan -y --providers=claude --scope=project

commands.name: search
commands.desc: Filter the catalog by id, name, description, or tags (bundled snapshot; works offline).

commands.name: install
commands.desc: Copy skill directories into the selected providers skills roots. Omit ids for interactive selection; non-interactive use needs -y and providers.

commands.name: update
commands.desc: Refresh installed skills by re-copying from the local skills source along the same write paths as install.

commands.name: list
commands.desc: List skills available in the catalog; add --installed to scan skills found under known harness paths.
commands.example:
npx openwisdom list
npx openwisdom list --installed

flags.desc: Comma-separated harness ids such as claude, cursor, agents, codex, gemini, and others. Controls which skills directories are written.
Non-interactive. Default scope is project; if providers are omitted, detect when possible, otherwise fall back to claude and agents.
project writes under the current project (see --cwd); global writes under the home harness path when that provider supports it.
Overwrite an existing SKILL.md when content hashes differ.
Print the install plan only; do not write files.
Project root used for project scope installs.
Skip default install of catalog references linked from a scenario.
Disable anonymous install-success heat reporting for this process.

mcpBody: MCP is the same core over local stdio tools for agents such as Claude Code and Cursor. It remains a package manager—not a chatbot and not a model caller.
Write tools require explicit providers; they never hang waiting for a TTY multiselect. Recommended flow: openwisdom_detect_providers then search/list then optional dryRun install then install.
cliPage.mcpDevNote: Optional for contributors: build packages/mcp from the monorepo, then point OPENWISDOM_SKILLS_ROOT at the local skills tree:

mcpTools.name: openwisdom_search
mcpTools.desc: Search the catalog and return a structured skill list.

mcpTools.name: openwisdom_install
mcpTools.desc: Install skills; providers is required. force, dryRun, and related semantics match the CLI/core contract.

mcpTools.name: openwisdom_update
mcpTools.desc: Refresh installed skills along the same write paths as install.

mcpTools.name: openwisdom_detect_providers
mcpTools.desc: Read-only detection of likely harness paths on the machine or project; no disk writes.

cliPage.mcpConfigNote: stdio MCP shape below. Prefer npx -y openwisdom-mcp. On Windows, if spawn fails, try cmd /c npx -y openwisdom-mcp. Contributors may point command at a monorepo node entry instead.
cliPage.mcpConfigExample:
claude mcp add --transport stdio openwisdom -- npx -y openwisdom-mcp

# Cursor / Claude Desktop and similar (stdio)
# mcpServers.openwisdom.command = npx
# mcpServers.openwisdom.args = -y, openwisdom-mcp
# optional env: OPENWISDOM_NO_TELEMETRY=1
# optional env: OPENWISDOM_SKILLS_ROOT=absolute path to local skills/
cliPage.telemetryBody: After a successful write to all selected providers, CLI/MCP may POST an anonymous install-success event. Heat is a side channel and never mutates SKILL.md. Network errors, timeouts, or a missing report URL are ignored; install exit codes stay fail-open. Opt out with --no-telemetry, OPENWISDOM_NO_TELEMETRY=1, or CI=true. Full collection scope and purpose are on the privacy page.

agentsPage.title: Agents and harness paths
agentsPage.lede: Where Openwisdom skills land depends on your coding agent. Paths below are typical / common roots used by our CLI and install tools—confirm against your agent current docs if something does not show up.
whatBody: Openwisdom installs skill folders into agent skills directories. Analysis always runs in your agent and model budget—not as a hosted chat on this site.
CLI and MCP write using a provider path table (ids such as claude, cursor, codex, agents). Manual copy uses the same roots when you place folders yourself.
Paths can drift across agent versions. Treat the matrix as typical defaults; when unsure, use the Install hub manual steps or run provider detection with the CLI/MCP.
agentsPage.matrixIntro: Each row is a provider id our tools understand. Project paths are relative to the repo root; global paths are under your home directory. Skill folders go one level deeper: e.g. .claude/skills/macro-scan/SKILL.md.
matrixRows: Global: ~/.claude/skills. Alias: claude-code. Confirm with Claude Code docs if your version differs.
Global: ~/.cursor/skills. Some setups also read portable .agents/skills—use agents if you prefer that root.
Cross-harness portable root (alias: portable). Global: ~/.agents/skills. Useful when multiple tools share agents-style skills.
Shares the project path with agents (install dedupes). Global typical: ~/.codex/skills. Confirm with current Codex docs.
Alias: copilot. Global typical: ~/.copilot/skills. Layout can vary by Copilot product/version—if detection fails, use manual install.
No guaranteed path. Copy the skill folder into the directory your agent documents, or open an Issue with agent name and version.
scopesBody: Install scope chooses which root the skill is written under. Pick project when the skill should travel with a repository; pick global when you want it on this machine for all workspaces that harness supports.
agentsPage.projectBody: Writes under the current working directory (repo root), e.g. project-root/.claude/skills/skill-id. Best for team-shared or repo-local workflows. Commit only if your team intends to share those files.
agentsPage.globalBody: Writes under your home directory, e.g. ~/.claude/skills/skill-id or provider-specific global roots such as ~/.codex/skills. Not every harness path is identical for project and global—Codex and Copilot use different global folders than their project paths.

troubleshootItems.q: The agent does not list my newly installed skill
troubleshootItems.a: Confirm the folder sits under the harness skills root (matrix above), that SKILL.md is present, and that the slug matches the catalog id. Reload or restart the agent. Paths may differ by version—check your agent docs or reinstall with an explicit --providers value.

troubleshootItems.q: How do I know which providers I have?
troubleshootItems.a: Interactive CLI install can detect common harness markers, and MCP exposes a read-only openwisdom_detect_providers tool. You can also inspect your project for folders like .claude, .cursor, or .agents, or install manually into the matching path.

troubleshootItems.q: I use Codex and agents together—will files duplicate?
troubleshootItems.a: Both use .agents/skills for project installs. Openwisdom dedupes shared write targets so one folder is written once. Global Codex still uses ~/.codex/skills.

troubleshootItems.q: My agent is not in the matrix
troubleshootItems.a: Use manual install: copy the skill folder into the path your agent expects. Prefer that over inventing a path. The Install hub always documents the manual path.

troubleshootItems.q: Does Openwisdom run analysis for me after install?
troubleshootItems.a: No. Install only places skill packages. You invoke the skill inside your agent; there is no hosted analysis session on this site.

changelogPage.title: Changelog

changelogPage.sourceBody: This page summarizes what is in the repo. Full diffs, plans, and Releases live on GitHub. We do not invent install counts or user numbers.
changelogPage.githubNote: Commits, Issues, and Releases are the authoritative change log. Package versions track on npm as openwisdom and openwisdom-mcp.

agentPrompt.gettingStarted:
You are helping the user with Openwisdom, an open-source social-science agent skills library (scenario workflows + discipline reference cards). Skills install into coding agents; analysis runs in THIS agent session—not on a hosted Openwisdom chat.

Hard constraints:
- Openwisdom does not host analysis, browser chat sessions, or a run tool that calls models.
- CLI and MCP are package managers only: search / install / update / list.
- Do not invent hosted-chat features or fabricate install counts.

Concrete steps:
1. Align on product boundary: the catalog site discovers skills; install only places skill folders into harness paths; analysis happens here in this agent.
2. Install path: packages are on npm. Prefer npx openwisdom install. Optional alternatives: GitHub repo Retr0-rgb-lab/Openwisdom, monorepo packages for contributors, or manual copy into the agent skills path (see the Install hub).
3. Install the official scenario skill macro-scan: npx openwisdom install macro-scan (or copy the macro-scan folder from the skills tree into the harness skills root).
4. Invoke macro-scan in this session per SKILL.md (name or description match). Run once on the user's real material.
5. Verify: the skill folder exists at the expected path (e.g. project-root/.claude/skills/macro-scan/SKILL.md); the agent can load it; one structured, reviewable analysis draft is produced—not a website chat transcript.

Success criteria:
- skill-id directory and SKILL.md exist on disk
- Agent loads the skill instructions and completes one analysis pass
- No claim that analysis happened on a hosted site or external hosted session
agentPrompt.cli:
You are helping the user with Openwisdom CLI and MCP package-manager surfaces. Openwisdom is a social-science agent skills library. The CLI is for humans in a terminal; MCP tools are for agent sessions. Both share catalog and install semantics.

Hard constraints:
- CLI and MCP are package managers only—they do not call LLMs, run analysis, or need model API keys.
- Command surface is fixed: search / install / update / list. No run command, no hosted sessions.
- Packages are on npm as openwisdom and openwisdom-mcp (0.1.0+). Monorepo and GitHub / manual paths remain optional for contributors and fallbacks.
- Never call LLM APIs as Openwisdom. Do not fabricate install counts.

CLI essentials:
- search: filter catalog by id, name, description, or tags (bundled snapshot; offline-capable).
- install: copy skill directories into selected providers skills roots; non-interactive needs -y and providers.
- update: refresh installed skills along the same write paths as install.
- list: list catalog skills; --installed scans known harness paths.

Common flags: --providers (e.g. claude,cursor,agents,codex,gemini), --scope project|global, -y / --yes, --force, --dry-run, --cwd, --no-deps, --no-telemetry.

Example: npx openwisdom install macro-scan -y --providers=claude --scope=project

MCP essentials:
- Tools: openwisdom_search, openwisdom_list, openwisdom_install (providers required), openwisdom_update, openwisdom_detect_providers (read-only).
- Write tools require explicit providers; never hang waiting for a TTY multiselect.
- Config shape (stdio): command npx, args -y, openwisdom-mcp. Optional for contributors: monorepo node packages/mcp/dist/mcp.js with OPENWISDOM_SKILLS_ROOT set.
- Recommended flow: detect_providers → search/list → optional dryRun → install.

Success criteria:
- User understands CLI/MCP as package managers, not analysis engines
- You can give executable search/install/list/update or MCP-equivalent steps
- You do not claim model calls or invent install counts
agentPrompt.agents:
You are helping the user install Openwisdom skills into the correct coding-agent harness paths. Analysis always runs in this agent session; install only writes skill folders.

Hard constraints:
- Do not invent hosted analysis.
- Paths can drift across agent versions; the matrix below is typical defaults—confirm against current agent docs.
- When unsure, use manual copy or provider detection; do not invent paths.

Typical project path matrix (relative to project-root):
- claude (Claude Code): .claude/skills; global ~/.claude/skills
- cursor: .cursor/skills; global ~/.cursor/skills; some setups also read .agents/skills
- agents (portable): .agents/skills; global ~/.agents/skills
- codex: project shares .agents/skills with agents (install dedupes); global typical ~/.codex/skills
- github / copilot: .github/skills; global typical ~/.copilot/skills
- gemini: .gemini/skills; global ~/.gemini/skills
- unknown harness: manual install per that agent docs

Scope:
- project: write under the current repo root, e.g. project-root/.claude/skills/skill-id
- global: write under the home harness root; Codex and Copilot global folders may differ from project paths

Troubleshooting:
1. Agent does not list the skill: confirm folder under the skills root, SKILL.md present, slug matches catalog id, then reload/restart the agent; or reinstall with explicit --providers.
2. Detect providers: use interactive CLI install or openwisdom_detect_providers; or inspect for .claude / .cursor / .agents markers.
3. Codex and agents together: project path is deduped to one write; Codex global still uses ~/.codex/skills.

Success criteria:
- Correct write path for the user's chosen harness
- skill-id directory and SKILL.md verifiable on disk
- Clear steps to reload the agent so the skill becomes visible
agentPrompt.authoring:
You are helping the user author and contribute an Openwisdom skill. Openwisdom is a social-science agent skills library. Content truth lives in the git skills/ tree; the site and CLI share a generated catalog index.

Hard constraints:
- Community contributions use scope=community and PRs into skills/community/. Do not claim official unless a maintainer invites changes under official/.
- Do not invent metadata only on the website; a skill unit is a directory plus SKILL.md.
- Heat/stats never write into SKILL.md.
- Site UI may be bilingual; skill body language follows the contributor—do not force bilingual bodies.
- Analysis still runs in the user's agent; contributions are installable packages, not hosted chat.

Skill unit:
- One directory = one skill: required SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + Markdown), optional assets/.
- layer: scenario (full analysis workflow) or reference (reusable theory card).
- Scenarios should cite references instead of stuffing textbooks into workflows.

Frontmatter fields (per repo schema):
- name: stable kebab-case id aligned with the directory
- description: short text for agent and catalog discovery
- layer: scenario | reference
- scope: community for community PRs
- disciplines: e.g. psychology, sociology, history, political-science, economics
- language: body language (zh / en / etc.)
- tags, version, references: discovery, versioning, and citation links

Writing:
- scenario: when to use / not use, inputs, executable steps, output structure, bias and evidence checks, cite references.
- reference: short definition, applicability bounds, common misuses, reviewable points; keep card-sized.

Contribution steps:
1. Fork Retr0-rgb-lab/Openwisdom and clone.
2. Create skill-id/ with SKILL.md under skills/community/.
3. Fill frontmatter and body; self-check against schema/templates.
4. Open a PR describing intent and bounds; do not edit official/ unless invited.

Success criteria:
- Correct directory layout; frontmatter indexable by the catalog
- scope=community; no false official claim
- PR targets skills/community/ and is reviewable
